summary: Discrepancy: tool-invoke line items vs aggregated token lines producing ~12% higher May invoice
description:
Issue summary: Customer NeonRetail reported their finalized invoice for May shows a ~12% surplus compared to the Console estimate. The delta originates from a set of tool-invoke line items that, when summed with the token-level generation lines, produce double counting.

Impact: Single enterprise account; month-end finalized invoice already paid. Customer requests an itemized explanation and corrective credit or refund. Business impact: invoice is material to their monthly budget for the retail season (estimated $18k delta).

Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated tenancy with hosted fallback enabled.

Observed behaviour: Many streaming chat sessions that used function/tool-calls show both a tool-invoke per-invocation line item (per-invoke rate) and the generation token lines that appear to include the same tool payload tokens. The aggregation logic should classify tool payload tokens under the tool-invoke charge only (not also under main-request token billing).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use a streaming session with function calls enabled.
2) Trigger a tool call that returns ~1.2k tokens of structured JSON.
3) Finish the stream; ensure the session is tracked with invocation_id present in request metadata.
4) Observe postback: two meter entries are emitted (tool_invoke.v1 and chat.tokens.v1) for the same logical work.
5) Run billing-aggregator for that hour window and inspect the output lines for duplication.
logs:
Relevant sample usage IDs: nr-usage-20260512-AB12, nr-usage-20260518-XY99.
Postback snapshots: s3://redwood-postbacks/prod/us-east/2026-05/XX/ (customer token masked).
Billing-aggregator log excerpt (2026-05-18 03:12 UTC): "[WARN] duplicate-classification: invocation_id present, but tool payload tokens also assigned to chat.tokens.v1"
API gateway trace IDs: trace-77dbc2f3, trace-9a1e4c8a.
Attached console screenshots requested by customer were included in initial ticket email.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support (Laila) collected usage IDs and escalated to Billing Eng.
On 2026-03-06 Ravi reproduced locally using a synthetic stream that invoked an inline tool returning ~1k tokens; the postback pipeline generated two separate meter events: one for the tool_invoke (correct) and one for chat.tokens (incorrect).
Hypothesis: aggregator dedup logic uses (request_id, api_key) but not invocation_id for streaming postbacks—when streaming is cut into partial postbacks, the later chunk that contains the tool payload does not carry the dedupe flag and gets classified as chat tokens.
Query run: SELECT count(*) FROM meters WHERE invocation_id IS NOT NULL AND meter_type = 'chat.tokens.v1' AND created_at BETWEEN '2026-05-01' AND '2026-05-31' AND customer = 'neonretail' -> 4,312 lines.
Found a regression introduced by infra PR github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2621 which modified streaming postback composition to dedupe on request_id only (PR reverted in staging).
Linked incident: INT-789 contains a related alert where an aggregated postback window truncated invocation_id in rare partial-chunk flows.
resolution:
Root cause: edge-case in postback composition + billing-aggregator dedup logic where streaming partials lost invocation_id in one chunk, resulting in the same tokens being billed twice (as tool_invoke and as chat.token).
Fix deployed: 2026-03-09 - patched postback composer to always include invocation_id in partials and updated billing-aggregator dedupe to prefer invocation_id when present. Rollout: canary -> 10% -> 100% over 6 hours in prod-us-east.
Customer remediation: Issued one-time invoice credit of $2,200 to correct the May overcharge (applied to NeonRetail main account; refund processed per payment method on file).
Status: Credits applied and customer acknowledged receipt. Internal rollback not required; forward fix deployed to all regions.
workaround: Until fix, customers could: 1) disable streaming partials for tool calls and use synchronous tool invocation (reduces risk), or 2) include invocation_id explicitly in request metadata to help dedupe. We communicated this as temporary guidance in a direct support note on 2026-03-06.
next_steps:
1) Post-deploy monitor for May-equivalent window to ensure no residual duplicate meters for NeonRetail (owner: Ravi).
2) Add automated integration test that simulates streaming + tool invocation and checks postback dedupe (owner: QA).
3) Add console alert for >1% month-over-month divergence between Console estimate and finalized invoice at account level (owner: Billing).
4) Follow-up with Finance to confirm refund bookkeeping and provide memo ID FIN-2026-0310 (owner: Finance Ops).
